_doc: Recall test fixture for app/retrieval.retrieve(). Tunable + reviewable — edit cases here, never in the script.
Probes the diagnosed bug: GENERIC self/identity questions sit at cosine 0.58-0.72 (distance probe), ABOVE the
0.55 topic gate, so the topic tier returns nothing and the user falls back on CORE.
case.type:   'probe' = generic question that SHOULD fail at baseline (tests the bug).
'guard' = direct-phrasing question that already passes via topic; must keep passing after the fix.
case.expected_fail (true): a generic question whose only answer is a BELOW-FLOOR fact (salience < 4). CORE
breadth (salience>=4) will NOT surface it and the phrasing is measured ABOVE the 0.55 gate so topic can't
either. Reported XFAIL when it fails (as designed); tracked for the Part 2 re-score. This keeps the
relationship seam VISIBLE so a clean identity-fact pass can't paper over it. Verified distance: 'tell me
about my relationships' -> nearest relationship fact 0.574, nearest Maddie fact 0.584 (both > 0.55).
must_land_in_core: substrings that, AFTER the fix, must appear in the CORE tier specifically — proves the
>=4 essentials survive CORE_LIMIT and are not truncated by updated_at ordering. (At baseline they are
absent, since CORE is salience==5 + identity/preference — that's the before/after contrast.)
Every 'expect' substring is verified present in the live memories table (read-only SELECT, Report 1).
Match is case-insensitive substring against concatenated content of the core+topic facts retrieve() returns.

identity s4: Nate is a college student

identity s4: Nate is a former hockey player (former, but the only sport/hobby fact at >=4)

relationship s2: Nate's girlfriend's name is Maddie -- BELOW-FLOOR relationship fact, tracked for Part 2. Measured 0.574/0.584 > 0.55 gate so topic cannot rescue it; CORE breadth (>=4) cannot either. EXPECTED-FAIL until the Part 2 re-score.
preference s3: Nate's favorite color is purple (direct phrasing -> topic tier; regression guard)

relationship s2: same Maddie fact, asked DIRECTLY -> topic tier catches it (0.543 < 0.55); regression guard
